full_judgment:
3. The opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptee resisted the pre-emption alleging that the case is barred by limitation, and inadequate deposit of consideration money. It is alleged that the heirs of one Abdul Bari Chowdhury auction purchased the case holding along with other lands of the concerned Khatians vide Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1945 on 28-6-1956 and the vendors of the petitioner were judgment debtor Nos. 9 and 10 in that Money Execution Case. The alleged purchase of the petitioner by the Kobala dated 25-4-1950 is fictitious, fraudulent, collusive and a mere paper transaction and the entire land of the case khatian along with other land auction sold were within the knowledge of the petitioner and for non-taking of any steps for annulling the said auction the purchase right of the petitioner including the right, title and possession' of the degree-holder party has been extinguished and, as such, the petitioner has no subsisting interest conveying any right to claim pre- emption in the case land. It is also the specific case of the pre-emptee that he purchased the case land along with other lands from Zaharul Haque Chowdhury and others by a registered kabala dated 30-4-1969 and got possession thereof in due course and the petitioner was all along aware of his purchase of the case land. So, alleged knowledge of the transfer from Dilal Ahmed on 1-11-1970 for the first time is false and fictitious. 

 4. During the trial learned Assistant Judge held that the case is neither barred by limitation nor bad for short deposit of consideration which was made in proportion to the case land comprising 1.01 acres of land out of 3.80 acres of the case holding. The learned Assistant Judge allowed pre-emption on the finding of petitioner's prima facie title acquired by the Exhibit 1 for not being attached by the impugned auction sale. On appeal the lower Appellate Court reversed the judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge in terms of its judgment and order with a direction upon the parties for establishment of their title in the lands of the case khatian in regular title suit in the light of the observation made in the body of the judgment wherein it has been held that the petitioner stepped in to the shoes of his vendor i.e. the judgment debtor Nos. 9 and 10, whose title and possession has been extinguished by the auction sale.
